title: Civil War to Glorious Revolution Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll watch a king lose his head and parliament become supreme.
meta_desc: GCSE History — Civil War, Cromwell and the Glorious Revolution.
final_note: You learned how 1649 and 1688 made Parliament supreme.

concepts.def: King executed in January 1649 after Civil War
Charles II returned to the throne in 1660
1688 — William of Orange replaced James II
1689 law making Parliament supreme over the monarch

walkthroughs.body_html:
Charles I clashed with Parliament over money and religion.

He tried to arrest 5 MPs in January 1642 — and Civil War broke out. Cromwell's New Model Army won at Naseby (1645). Charles was tried for treason and beheaded on 30 January 1649.

Britain became a Commonwealth. From 1653 Cromwell ruled as Lord Protector.

After his death in 1658 the Protectorate collapsed. In 1660 Parliament invited Charles II back. He kept the Crown weaker than his father's — but his brother James II tried to restore Catholic power.

In 1688 seven nobles invited William of Orange to invade.

James II fled. William and Mary became joint monarchs, accepting the 1689 Bill of Rights: no taxes without Parliament, no standing army in peacetime, free speech in Parliament. The Crown was finally constitutional.
